name: Wallfahrtsort St. Georgenberg
kurzbeschreibung: St. Georgenberg near Stans: Tyrol's oldest pilgrimage site perched on an 898-metre cliff top, featuring the spectacular Hohe Brücke and rock monastery dating from 950.
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied pilgrimage destination St. Georgenberg is boldly perched on a steep, isolated rock pinnacle at 898 metres above sea level in the Georgental valley above the village of Stans in the Unterinntal. As the oldest attested pilgrimage destination in all of Tyrol, this idyllic mountain sanctuary looks back on more than a millennium of Christian devotion and monastic heritage. Framed by the soaring limestone cliffs of the Karwendel Nature Park, the pilgrimage site can only be reached on foot – a circumstance that preserves its extraordinary atmosphere of tranquillity, contemplation, and unspoilt alpine nature.

History & Hohe Brücke

The origins of the shrine date back to the mid-10th century: around the year 950, the nobleman Rathold von Aibling retreated to this isolated rocky wilderness as a hermit. Companions soon joined him, and in 1138 Pope Innocent II elevated the community to a Benedictine abbey. For centuries, emperors, princes, and hundreds of thousands of pilgrims travelled to venerate the Schmerzhafte Muttergottes (Our Lady of Sorrows) and the famous Heilig-Blut-Wunder (Holy Blood Miracle), which according to tradition occurred during a Holy Mass in the early 14th century. Several devastating fires, rockfalls, and destruction by an avalanche in 1705 ultimately forced the Benedictine monks to relocate their monastery down into the valley at Vomp in 1708, where the baroque Stift Fiecht was established; St. Georgenberg, however, remained a vibrant pilgrimage sanctuary. The present pilgrimage church of St. Georg and Jakobus was built between 1732 and 1735 in a simple Tyrolean baroque style. An absolute masterpiece of historic civil engineering is the spectacular Hohe Brücke: a covered timber bridge first constructed in 1497 and rebuilt in the 17th century, spanning roughly 40 metres across the rocky Georgenbach gorge at dizzying heights, remaining to this day the only access route to the rock plateau.

Visit & Getting There

The pilgrimage church of St. Georgenberg is open daily year-round free of charge for pilgrims and hikers (admission is free). The historic inn Wallfahrtsgasthaus St. Georgenberg on the rock plateau welcomes guests daily from early May to late October with traditional Tyrolean cuisine (limited opening hours on weekends in winter). As no public road leads up to the rock, the journey always requires a hike. Hiking route 1 (standard path): from the Weng car park near Stans or from Fiecht via a paved and gravelled forest road gently climbing over the Hohe Brücke (walking time approx. 1 to 1.25 hours). Hiking route 2 (scenic gorge route): from the centre of Stans through the spectacular Wolfsklamm via 354 wooden steps along roaring waterfalls up to the monastery (gorge admission fee applies, approx. €6.00 for adults). By public transport: take the ÖBB S-Bahn to Stans or Schwaz railway station, then continue by regional bus or on foot to the starting point.

Tips

The forest access road crossing the Hohe Brücke is wide and well maintained, making it suitable for all-terrain pushchairs and active walkers; by contrast, the route through the Wolfsklamm demands surefootedness and sturdy mountain boots. Take a seat on the sunny terrace of the pilgrimage inn and savour the homemade Tyrolean Kaspressknödel while admiring views of the towering rock formation.
